rows.name: TMPDIR

problems.statement: `bin/ci/background-check.sh` and `bin/ci/resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh` put their files below it when `RUNNER_TEMP` is unset or empty.
problems.code_says: background-check.sh checks BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR first, then RUNNER_TEMP, then TMPDIR, then /tmp. The row leaves out BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR for that script.

notes: All 12 rows are in section 7, so no row has a For cell. Convention question for the owner of the file: in GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITHUB_API_URL, GITHUB_ENV and GITHUB_EVENT_NAME only test code sets the name (bin/ci/test-lint-full-rejection.sh:46, bin/ci/test_lint_diagnostics.py:65, bin/ci/test_hf_cache.py:232, bin/ci/nix-cache/test_cache.py:307, bin/ci/test-resolve-apt-channel.sh:11, bin/slice-tests/test_bench_refresh_workflow.py:37). I kept 'Reads' in the Tron cell, as the other rows of table 7.2 do (for example GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and GITHUB_REPOSITORY). The column definition ('Tron code sets it, for itself or for a child process') read word for word gives 'Reads and sets' for these rows, and table 7.1 does count test files as setters (CDPATH, XDG_DATA_HOME). One rule for both tables is needed. TMPDIR: the 40-word limit left no room for one more effect: bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py puts its socket directory below TMPDIR and stops with an error when the socket path is longer than its limit (bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py:127). CI: the cell says nothing about make for the same reason; with a non-empty CI, make prints no warning about a run outside nix develop (GNUmakefile:1) and make lint does not skip Rust formatting on a missing cargo (GNUmakefile:856). USER: make sets CCACHE_DIR from USER only when CCACHE_DIR is not set (GNUmakefile:102); the CCACHE_DIR row holds that fact.
